sources.name: Enron Email Dataset
sources.authoritative_source: Carnegie Mellon University School of Computer Science (https://www.cs.cmu.edu/~enron/)
sources.description: Historical corporate email communications from approximately 150 senior management employees at Enron Corporation, released by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) during its investigation and subsequently prepared for research by MIT and CMU.
sources.license: Public investigatory record released for research (no explicit formal open-source license grant)

unlabeled_corporate_correspondence.rationale: unlabeled legitimate/business corpus -> benign: This is a modeling assumption for the MAILTRACE training taxonomy, not an original threat label supplied by Enron.

sources.verification_notes: FERC investigatory public record made available for research; CMU redacted certain sensitive personal and financial information per requests of former employees. Unlabeled legitimate/business corpus -> benign mapping is a modeling assumption for the MAILTRACE training taxonomy, not an original threat label supplied by Enron.
sources.provenance_notes: Publicly released FERC investigatory record hosted by CMU. Primary source for legitimate business email communication without security indicators. Note: Not natively labeled benign.
limitations: Unlabeled legitimate/business corpus mapped to benign as a modeling assumption; not natively labeled benign.
Historical corporate email from 1999-2002; formatting and headers differ from modern email ecosystems.
No formal open-source license grant from FERC or CMU; distributed as an investigatory research release.

sources.name: Apache SpamAssassin Public Corpus
sources.description: Benchmark email corpus provided by the Apache SpamAssassin project for spam filter evaluation, consisting of easy_ham, hard_ham, and spam archives.
sources.license: Apache SpamAssassin testing corpus / donated user email (software is Apache 2.0; individual donated emails lack separate license grants)

easy_ham.rationale: Verified non-spam personal and business email donated for filter testing.

hard_ham.rationale: Legitimate non-spam emails with complex formatting or headers; non-adversarial.

spam.rationale: Commercial bulk spam (UCE) cannot be defensibly mapped to phishing or BEC without specific credential-theft or impersonation evidence. Remains unresolved and rejected to prevent class contamination.

sources.verification_notes: Corpus intended by Apache SpamAssassin for spam filter evaluation and testing. Only easy_ham and hard_ham represent legitimate emails. The spam partition is unresolved and rejected because commercial bulk spam cannot be safely mapped to phishing or suspicious without specific threat indicators.
sources.provenance_notes: Standard open spam benchmark. Only ham archives are eligible for benign training; generic bulk spam remains unresolved and rejected.
limitations: Spam category remains unresolved and rejected from training to prevent label noise.
Corpus dates from 2002-2005; does not reflect modern threat vectors.
Donated email archives lack individual copyright releases.

sources.name: Nazario Phishing Corpus
sources.description: Longitudinal security research collection of real-world phishing emails containing authentic credential harvesting lures, brand impersonation, and deceptive landing links collected between 2004 and 2024.
sources.license: No explicit license provided on distribution site (public research archive of adversarial emails)

phishing.rationale: Confirmed authentic phishing emails targeting user credentials.

sources.verification_notes: Longitudinal archival collection of raw phishing emails collected via honeypots between 2005 and 2024. Contains authentic adversarial credential lures and fraudulent links. The distribution site monkey.org does not provide a formal license.
sources.provenance_notes: Verified security research collection referenced across academic anti-phishing literature. Raw adversarial email telemetry without formal license grant.
limitations: No explicit software or data license provided on monkey.org.
Contains raw malicious URLs, dead phishing links, and deceptive sender domains.
Total sample count is unverified prior to downloading and parsing individual mbox files.

sources.name: BEC-2 Research Corpus
sources.authoritative_source: Rohit Dube, UC Berkeley (Preprint: 'Building a Business Email Compromise Research Dataset with Large Language Models', Oct 2024)
sources.description: Academic Business Email Compromise research dataset containing 279 generated BEC emails based on real-world BEC examples, created using an LLM-based generation system.
sources.license: Unverified / Author distribution upon research request

bec.rationale: Generated BEC scenarios. Blocked from training pending verified license and explicit model governance approval.

sources.verification_notes: Contains 279 synthetic BEC emails generated by an LLM based on variations of real-world BEC scenarios. While validated with human analyst agreement scores, samples are researcher-generated rather than authentic mailbox telemetry. Must never be represented as authentic historical emails. No public open-source license is verified.
sources.provenance_notes: Generated from real-world BEC examples using LLMs. Not authentic collected mailbox corpus. Distributed via research preprint author contact.
limitations: Public BEC data is substantially more limited than general legitimate/phishing email data. BEC-2 provides 279 generated samples based on real-world BEC examples rather than a large authentic mailbox corpus.
Provenance: LLM-generated variations, not authentic historical mailbox records.
License and distribution unverified; requires direct research contact.

sources.name: IWSPA APWG Phishing Corpus
sources.authoritative_source: Anti-Phishing Working Group (APWG) / IWSPA Shared Task (https://apwg.org/resources/)
sources.description: Anti-Phishing Working Group (APWG) shared research corpus for email security competitions and academic benchmarks.
sources.license: Restricted APWG Member Agreement / Institutional NDA Required

phishing.rationale: Requires APWG institutional agreement before ingestion.

legitimate.rationale: Requires APWG institutional agreement before ingestion.

sources.verification_notes: Restricted institutional access. Requires signed institutional research agreement and membership with APWG. No automated download permitted.
sources.provenance_notes: Restricted institutional access / agreement required. Marked allowed_for_training=false. No automated download allowed.
limitations: Requires APWG membership / institutional data use agreement.
Cannot be downloaded or distributed automatically.
